newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei end firm but 19,000 target recedes.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei end firm but 19,000 target recedes.

text.p: Late buying of blue chips on the underlying cash market lifted SIMEX Nikkei futures by the close of Wednesday's trade, but dealers said the market did not show enough upside momentum to reach 19,000 points this week.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract ended 125 points up at 18,605 after hitting a high of 18,645.

Dealers said the market had opened on a relatively bearish note on lingering concerns about Japan's financial sector after Moody's Investors Service said on Tuesday it had placed its senior debt ratings for three Japanese banks under review for a possible downgrade.
"Technically also, it was looking quite overbought. So the market had to correct," said a trader at a Japanese house.

He said the March Nikkei was unlikely to extend its late gains significantly in the near term, and the 19,000 target that many analysts were calling for earlier this week looked like an increasingly remote prospect.

"There's been no good news. The upside looks very limited. I would still sell on rallies towards 18,700," he said. The market's inability to remain above 18,600 earlier in the week sent a poor signal, he added.
The March MSCI Taiwan index contract ended at 324.2 against its opening 323.0 as Taipei stocks rebounded after Tuesday's sharp falls. Market turnover was 721 lots.
